test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2021: Official Paper (Held On : 26 May 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

You have lost your note book.

options.text: Your note book have been lost.
Your note book has been lost.

solution:
The correct answer is "**Your note book has been lost.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• There are a few things to keep in mind before changing a sentence from **active to passive voice.**
 
• We can omit the subject in the passive voice if the sentence is meaningful without it.
 
• In the given sentence, the subject pronoun "**your**" modifies the meaning of the entire sentence so we don't need to use another relative pronoun for the sentence.
 
• The **object **of the **active **voice becomes the **subject **of the **passive voice**.
 
• In the given sentence, "**notebook**" is the **subject **of the sentence in the passive voice.
 
• The given sentence is in the **present perfect tense. **So we need to use "has been" when changing the sentence from active to passive voice.
 
• We need to use the **past particle form of "be"** in the given sentence as it becomes the **main verb **of the sentence. We always use the past participle form of the main verb in passive voice." **Been" **is the past participle of "be".
 
• In the given sentence, we need to use the auxiliary verb "**has**" for the subject-verb agreement as the sentence begins with the singular subject "**your notebook**".

Hence, the correct answer is** option 2.**

**The correct sentence is: ***Your note book has been lost.*
